key_insight: Including all single particle–hole transitions in QMC barely changes excitation energies but is crucial for capturing exciton localization in low-density solid molecular hydrogen.
engineering_relevance: Predicting optical response and excitation-induced forces in compressed molecular hydrogen requires wave functions that capture localization, not just accurate excitation energies.
method: Model phase-I molecular hydrogen under increasing compression using QMC.
Compare single-orbital substitutions with multideterminant expansions containing all single particle–hole transitions.
Benchmark against BSE and TDDFT across nuclear configurations representing thermal and quantum fluctuations.
evidence_signal: Multideterminant QMC generally agrees with BSE on localization, transition dipoles, and excitation-induced forces, while TDDFT predicts more extended excitons; differences decrease under compression.
watch_item: Similar excitation energies can mask substantial errors in localization and response, with agreement varying across nuclear configurations.
paper_title: Excitons in solid molecular hydrogen from quantum Monte Carlo
